back: A policy of not joining either Cold War bloc and judging issues on their merits; the Non-Aligned Movement brought such states together.
Independent southern African states that opposed white-minority rule and supported liberation: first Angola, Botswana, Mozambique, Tanzania and Zambia, joined by Zimbabwe in 1980 and Namibia in 1990.
Apartheid South Africa's policy of weakening neighbouring states by raids, support for rebel groups such as RENAMO and attacks on transport routes.

front: What happened in Harare in September 1986?
back: The Non-Aligned Movement summit; Zimbabwe's leader became chairman of the movement until 1989.
The road, rail and pipeline route from Zimbabwe to Beira in Mozambique, guarded by Zimbabwean troops from 1982 until the Rome agreement of 1992.
A Commonwealth statement of principles on democracy and human rights, adopted at the Harare meeting in October 1991.

front: When did Zimbabwe send troops to the DRC?
back: August 1998, with Angola and Namibia, to support the government against rebels.

front: Why was Zimbabwe interested in the Beira Corridor?
back: As a landlocked country it needed a short route to the sea that did not rely on South Africa.

front: Why was Zimbabwe's foreign policy cautious towards South Africa?
back: It depended on South African railways and trade and risked raids and border closures if it allowed armed bases.
